schema.title: MutationCapsGateFixture
schema.description: 🐘️ The structural cap rule of the repository gates (audit F3) and its fixture. A leaf payload schema that caps its inverse rows (`definitions.boundedLeaf`: `x-semio-inverse-rows.bounded`) must be wrapped by a non-generic `#[derive(Mutations)]` aggregate of its own artifact, because only then the derive emits the payload law that holds the leaf to its declared rows. The fixture plants leaves (directory, aggregate variant, payload schema) and aggregate sources per case and lists the directories the rule refuses as `capLawMissing`.

boundedLeaf.description: A leaf payload schema that declares a positive integer cap on its inverse rows.

schema.title: FaultNoticesGateFixture
schema.description: The schema-fault-notice gate fixture (design §20.12): Rust snippets with the fault code sites both the token gate and the tree-sitter-rust oracle read, and one planted repository (plugin, plugin SDK, descriptor, framework table) whose files yield exactly the listed findings and one census row per owner (with its finding count overall and in scope), and exactly `scoped.findings` under one scope.

schema.title: MutationInputDeclarationsGateFixture
schema.description: 🎛️ The declaration rules of the schema-mutation-input-ui gate (design §22.8, §22.20) and the fixture that plants a case per rule. The gate measures what a mutation payload schema DECLARES about each input's UI element, apart from what the reader infers. `definitions.resolvedInput` is one leaf input with its merged `x-semio-ui`; the four input rule schemas (`numericDeclared`, `labelResolved`, `widgetDeclared`, `multilineControlled`) state when such an input conforms, and `leafShowsInput` when a leaf (`definitions.resolvedLeaf`) does — a strict Ajv evaluates them as the independent oracle of the hand-written gate. The fixture lists shared documents and cases: a payload schema, whether the leaf descriptor declares the leaf withdraw-only (`editable: false`; no rule judges it then), the control kinds a reader hands its inputs (present when the multi-line rule is armed), every declaration row the gate reads and every `[code, pointer]` finding.

source.description: Where one UI fact comes from: the input's own x-semio-ui (declared), the reader's inference from the field name or JSON type (inferred), or nowhere (absent).

pointer.description: The RFC 6901 pointer of an input in the payload; `/-` is an array item.

resolvedInput.description: One leaf input as an oracle resolves it: its key, settled JSON type, whether a label shows for it (no hidden input, no array item), whether the input-label glossary names its key, the x-semio-ui merged over its $ref chain (outer keys first) and the control kind a reader hands it (null when none).

resolvedLeaf.description: One mutation leaf as an oracle resolves it: whether its descriptor leaves it editable (`editable` absent or true) and how many top-level inputs its editor shows (hidden ones do not count).

leafShowsInput.description: Leaf rule (design §22.20): a leaf is either editable and shows at least one input, or its descriptor declares it withdraw-only (`"editable": false`) — never an editor with zero rows.

numericDeclared.description: Rule a: an interactive number — role value or none, widget slider, stepper, dial or none, no reference — declares its step or its snapping points (a non-empty snaps list or a snapSource).

labelResolved.description: Rule b: the label of a shown input resolves in every locale — the input-label glossary names its key (a legitimate source, design §6: such a label is counted as inferred, never refused), or its own x-semio-ui.label states every locale (the manifest's InputLabel).

widgetDeclared.description: Rule c: a declared widget is one of the strict vocabulary (the widget enum of the manifest's InputUi, which the vendor-annotation vocabulary registers for x-semio-ui).

multilineControlled.description: Rule d (design §22.7), armed once the reader maps the multiline presentation to a control: an input declared multiline is handed the multi-line control.

documents.description: Schema documents the cases reference across documents, each resolved by its $id.

editable.description: The leaf descriptor's `editable` member; false declares the leaf withdraw-only. Absent means editable.

controls.description: Pointer → control kind of the reader's descriptors; present when the case runs with the multi-line rule armed.

error.const: Repository JSON requires a serializable top-level value

schema.title: Node Native TypeScript Surface
schema.description: ✂️ The TypeScript Node loads without a bundler (strip-only): the package entries vite/vitest configs externalize, and the syntax vectors Node's type stripper and TypeScript's erasableSyntaxOnly must judge alike.

schema.title: Gherkin Feature description inline-code span extraction
MutationLeafIdentityVectors
schema.description: Language-agnostic vectors for structural mutation leaf identity: a directory is a mutation leaf when its own canonical descriptor names it as owner; a `🧫️fixtures/🧬️mutations/<leaf>` mirror and a `🧫️fixtures/<leaf>` or `🧫️fixtures/<leaf>-<scenario>` vector directory (leaf names compared without U+FE0F) inherit that proof from their schema-side owner, as does a vector's scenario child that holds a fixture bundle.

const.label: optional ! then [ then zero-or-more non-] code units then ]
const.destination: ( then one-or-more non-whitespace non-) code units
const.title: optional whitespace plus double-quoted zero-or-more non-quote code units
const.coordinates: UTF-16 destination-only half-open offsets; line/column count raw LF boundaries
const.ordering: inline then definitions then HTML; duplicates preserved
const.escapes: no new destination or title escape grammar
const.scope: source-only text scanner, not CommonMark document parsing

const.proof: emitted normalized values plus distinct raw parseLinkDestination spans; speculative helper calls are not links

schema.description: 🚧️ Vectors of the workspace-negation closure law: a throwaway workspace (files), one project, and per case its named inputs, whether every `!{workspaceRoot}/…` negation of the expanded `subject` input has a workspace positive, and the files Nx's hash planner plans for it (without nx.json and the project's project.json).

schema.title: TaxonomyScopeClosureFixture
schema.description: 🔐️ The closure of a taxonomy verification scope: a scope inside a mutation facet (below `<owner>/🧬️schema/🧬️mutations` or `<owner>/🧫️fixtures/🧬️mutations`, or a `🧬️schema` / `🧫️fixtures` directory that holds a `🧬️mutations`) is verified over `<owner>`, every other scope over itself. Each case lists the scope, the directories that hold a `🧬️mutations` child, and the closed scope.

workerOutcomes: workers must be a positive integer

const: workers must be a positive integer
